CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
2. Bupati is the Bupati of West Bangka.
3. Regional Apparatus of the Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies and Regional Technical Institutions.
4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection administrators in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to the victim physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other Community Organizations.
18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence include any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, and forcing a person to have sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

Article 15
(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the West Bangka Regency government through Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 4
(1) The Regent through regional apparatus establishes a community service work unit that functions as an Integrated Service Center (PPT).
(2) The Integrated Service Center (PPT) as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment.
(3) The Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (1) in implementing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence may coordinate with other Regional Apparatus.

Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(2) The mechanism for handling protection and services shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BANGKA REGENCY
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST BANGKA REGENCY
NUMBER 15 OF 2011
CONCERNING
COOPERATION IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER VII
SOURCES OF FUNDS
Article 16
(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence carried out by the regional apparatus of West Bangka Regency as referred to in article 4 paragraph (1) shall come from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of West Bangka Regency and/or may come from other legitimate sources.
(2) Other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be subject to supervision in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER III
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER VI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 14
(1) The West Bangka Regency Government in implementing protection for Women and Children Victims of violence, may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation may be carried out by individuals, groups or community organizations and/or Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) that are already legally established.

REGENT OF WEST BANGKA
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION ON COOPERATION IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

CHAPTER VIII
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 17
Other matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation, shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER X
CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 18
This Regional Regulation shall come into force from the date of enactment.
In order that every person shall know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of West Bangka Regency.
Enacted in Muntok on the date of 6 June 2011

RAMLI NGAD JUM
REGIONAL GAZETTE OF WEST BANGKA REGENCY YEAR 2011 NUMBER 2 SERIES E

HEAD OF BANGKA BARAT REGENCY,
stamp/signed Ust.H.ZUHRI M.SYAZALI Promulgated in Muntok on 6 June 2011

REGIONAL SECRETARY
WEST BANGKA REGENCY,
stamp/signed

(4) Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

Article 4
(1) The Regent through regional apparatus establishes a community service work unit that functions as an Integrated Service Center (PPT).

Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

CHAPTER VII
SOURCES OF FUNDS
Article 16
(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence carried out by the regional apparatus of West Bangka Regency as referred to in article 4 paragraph (1) shall come from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of West Bangka Regency and/or may come from other legitimate sources.

Article 17
Other matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation, shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER X
CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 18
This Regional Regulation shall come into force from the date of enactment.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence include any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, and forcing a person to have sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
2. Bupati is the Bupati of West Bangka.
3. Regional Apparatus of the Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies and Regional Technical Institutions.
4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection administrators in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to the victim physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(2) The mechanism for handling protection and services shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.

(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
2. Bupati is the Bupati of West Bangka.
3. Regional Apparatus of the Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies and Regional Technical Institutions.
4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection administrators in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to the victim physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other Community Organizations.
18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION ON COOPERATION IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

Article 15
(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the West Bangka Regency government through Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence include any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, and forcing a person to have sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(2) The mechanism for handling protection and services shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII
SOURCES OF FUNDS
Article 16
(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence carried out by the regional apparatus of West Bangka Regency as referred to in article 4 paragraph (1) shall come from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of West Bangka Regency and/or may come from other legitimate sources.
(2) Other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be subject to supervision in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 14
(1) The West Bangka Regency Government in implementing protection for Women and Children Victims of violence, may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation may be carried out by individuals, groups or community organizations and/or Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) that are already legally established.

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER VIII
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 17
Other matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation, shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 18

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.

4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection administrators in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to the victim physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(2) The mechanism for handling protection and services shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.

CHAPTER VII
SOURCES OF FUNDS
Article 16
(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence carried out by the regional apparatus of West Bangka Regency as referred to in article 4 paragraph (1) shall come from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of West Bangka Regency and/or may come from other legitimate sources.
(2) Other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be subject to supervision in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.

(3) Forms of sexual violence include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, and forcing a person to have sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

CHAPTER VI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 14
(1) The West Bangka Regency Government in implementing protection for Women and Children Victims of violence, may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation may be carried out by individuals, groups or community organizations and/or Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) that are already legally established.

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER VIII
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 17
Other matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation, shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 18

5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.

8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.

Article 5

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.

(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(2) The mechanism for handling protection and services shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
2. Bupati is the Bupati of West Bangka.
3. Regional Apparatus of the Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies and Regional Technical Institutions.
4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection administrators in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to the victim physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other Community Organizations.
18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

Article 15
(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the West Bangka Regency government through Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

Article 4
(1) The Regent through regional apparatus establishes a community service work unit that functions as an Integrated Service Center (PPT).

(3) The Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (1) in implementing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence may coordinate with other Regional Apparatus.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence include any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, and forcing a person to have sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Article 16

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 15
(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the West Bangka Regency government through Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.

HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5

SOURCES OF FUNDS

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
2. Bupati is the Bupati of West Bangka.
3. Regional Apparatus of the Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies and Regional Technical Institutions.
4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection administrators in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to the victim physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other Community Organizations.
18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(2) The mechanism for handling protection and services shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 15
(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the West Bangka Regency government through Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other Community Organizations.
18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

CHAPTER VI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 14
(1) The West Bangka Regency Government in implementing protection for Women and Children Victims of violence, may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation may be carried out by individuals, groups or community organizations and/or Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) that are already legally established.

Article 15
(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the West Bangka Regency government through Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

Article 4
(1) The Regent through regional apparatus establishes a community service work unit that functions as an Integrated Service Center (PPT).
(2) The Integrated Service Center (PPT) as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment.
(3) The Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (1) in implementing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence may coordinate with other Regional Apparatus.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.

Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(2) The mechanism for handling protection and services shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION

(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

SOURCES OF FUNDS
Article 16
(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence carried out by the regional apparatus of West Bangka Regency as referred to in article 4 paragraph (1) shall come from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of West Bangka Regency and/or may come from other legitimate sources.
(2) Other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be subject to supervision in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 17
Other matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation, shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

Article 9
(1) Health services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional governments, and the community, including private facilities, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance, and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of victims.
(3) Counseling is provided by social workers and volunteer companions by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding the victim’s rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.

HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5

CHAPTER II

Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.

Article 3
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and, in the best interests of the child, to children, in cases occurring in the household or in public.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) Forms of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) Forms of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) Forms of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and to provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) Forms of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include skills training services and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence include any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, and forcing a person to have sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
2. Bupati is the Bupati of West Bangka.
3. Regional Apparatus of the Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies and Regional Technical Institutions.
4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection administrators in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to the victim physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other Community Organizations.
18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice, as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency, whether the violence occurs in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children who are victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka where the violence occurs within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 4
(1) The Regent through regional apparatus establishes a community service work unit that functions as an Integrated Service Center (PPT).
(2) The Integrated Service Center (PPT) as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment.
(3) The Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (1) in implementing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence may coordinate with other Regional Apparatus.

(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.
